p: the dimness shall not be such: He comforts the Church again after these great threatenings promising to restore them to great glory in Messiah.

when at the first he lightly: With which Israel was punished, first by Tiglath-pilesar, which was a light scourge in respect to that which they suffered afterward by Shalmaneser, who carried the Israelites away captive.
the nations: While the Jews and Gentiles dwelt together by reason of those twenty cites, which Solomon gave to Hiram.
walked in darkness have seen a: Which were in captivity in Babylon and the prophets speaks of that thing which would come to pass 60 years later as though it were now done.
light: Meaning, the comfort of their deliverance.
light shined: This captivity and deliverance were figures of our captivity by sin and of our deliverance by Christ through the preaching of the Gospel, Mt 4:15,16.
multiplied the nation: Their number was greater when they went into captivity then when they returned but their joy was greater at their return, Hag 2:9.
yoke of his burden: You gave them perfect joy by delivering them, and by destroying the tyrants, that had kept them in cruel bondage, as you delivered them by Gideon from the Midianites, Jud 7:21.

with burning and fuel of fire: He speaks of the deliverance of his Church, which he has delivered miraculously from his enemies, but especially by the coming of Christ of whom he prophecies in the next verse.
Father: The author of eternity, and by whom the Church and every member of it will be preserved forever, and have immortal life.
The zeal of the LORD of: His singular love and care for his elect.
Israel: This is another prophecy against them of Samaria who were mockers and contemners of God's promises and menaces.
bricks have fallen down: We were but weak, when the enemy overcame us, but we will make ourselves so strong, that we will neither care for our enemies, nor fear God's threatenings.

Rezin against him: Rezin king of Syria, who was in league with Israel, was slain by the Assyrians, after whose death, Aram that is, the Syrians were against Israel, who on the other side were assailed by the Philistines.
Wickedness as a bellows kindles the fire of God's wrath which consumes all his obstinate enemies.
spare his brother: Though there was no foreign enemy, yet they will destroy one another.
flesh of his own arm: Their greediness will be insatiable, so that one brother will eat up another, as though he should eat his own flesh.
